GitHub LinkedIn

docs.title: About me
docs.text:
I'm currently a graduate student in Electrical Engineering at National Taiwan University, working in the Speech Processing and Machine Learning (SPML) Lab under Prof. Hung-Yi Lee. My research centers on large audio language models, Text-to-Speech, and bringing reasoning and reinforcement learning into speech systems.

I'm passionate about machine learning, speech processing, and real-world applications of deep learning. Feel free to connect! 🚀

docs.title: Experience
docs.text:
AI Research Intern — ASUS (Jul 2024 - Jun 2025)

  • Trained a large language model to directly generate Mimi codec representations, enabling an end-to-end TTS pipeline that bridges language modeling with speech synthesis.
  • Fine-tuned Gemma-3 into a reasoning model using multi-GPU distributed training.
  • Conducted experiments on StreamBench, comparing fine-tuning vs. in-context learning strategies.

HPC System Administrator — SPML Lab, NTU (Aug 2025 - Present)

  • Administer a Slurm-managed HPC cluster with 5 compute nodes and 30+ GPUs.
  • Manage the cluster OS environment on Arch Linux, including package maintenance, kernel upgrades, and system configuration.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
• ReasonTTS: Reasoning-Aligned Instructional Speech Generation (2025 - Present)

    A multi-hop reasoning framework that lets the TTS model self-refine its generated speech through iterative reasoning, with reinforcement learning integrated into the generation pipeline to improve quality and instruction-following.

  • HAHAHA: Humor-Aligned and Human-Aligned Hilarious Agent (2025 - Present)

    Uses real-world social-media engagement signals (e.g. "likes") as implicit human feedback to build a reward signal for humor generation, training a ranking-based reward model and applying PPO to align toward human-perceived funniness.
